programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: The worlds of windsurfing and funeral directing collide when a body is found washed up on the beach. With Joe along for the ride, Rose and Raj must find what connects them.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Three generations of the same family need help from Jules Hudson to find them a new, rural Norfolk home. In the kitty is £800,000 for a four-bedroom house, an annexe for Granny and enough land for a Shetland pony. Jules also needs a keen eye to spot some of the world’s rarest (and camera-shy) species of deer and antelope at a local safari park.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – William, Nicky, Abz, Chris and Charlotte – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

With music from Take That, performing their current single, Higher.

programme.title: Fall
programme.desc: A fast drop and a sudden stop await Becky (Grace Fulton) and Hunter (Virginia Gardner) as they find themselves trapped 2,000 feet up an abandoned radio tower in the desert. Highly trained and resourceful, these climbers marking the tragic passing of a friend were not ready for every eventuality. A series of unfortunate events see their gear and supplies taken from them, and as temperatures rise and vultures begin to circle, the chance of survival begins to fall rapidly. A heart-pounding tale of survival from the producers of 47 Meters Down, where sacrifice may just be the only way out.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Surrey, Sarah Moore is at Witley recycling centre, trawling the car boots in the hope of finding some potential gems in need of creative magic. Upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence are tested by a wooden cabinet in disrepair, four chairs in a mix of styles get a radical revamp from woodworker Martin Hough, whilst Sarah must think out of the box when she takes on a metal trunk full of vintage tools.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A creative couple from London want to leave city life behind in search of new adventures in Gloucestershire, and Chris Bavin is on hand to guide them. Along with presenting a lovely selection of houses, Chris also visits a local football club to check out for himself why it’s green by name and green by nature.

programme.title: Final Score

programme.title: The Famous Finish Line

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s that time of year again – Strictly returns to the home of ballroom dancing, the iconic Blackpool Tower, for a spectacular night of dancing. The show begins with a group performance from the entire cast and the legendary Basement Jaxx. Then, Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome our couples to the world-famous ballroom for their biggest performances of the competition. Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke have packed their paddles and will be sharing expert advice before the vote opens and you have your say. Which couple’s performance will be the talk of the tower?

programme.title: Michael McIntyre's The Wheel
programme.desc: Michael McIntyre hosts his hit game show packed with huge stars, big laughs and a giant spinning wheel. Can the contestants answer their way to a fortune? The celebrity experts in this episode are Italian Bach, Kerry Godliman, Trevor Nelson, Angela Scanlon, Alex Scott, Josh Widdicombe, Bez and Shaun Ryder.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Friedrich is ordered by his boss Schimmel to ramp up his efforts to locate Greta, believing she is the key to the Hermann Metzl case. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of seven Premier League games, including leaders Arsenal, who travel to Newcastle. Manchester City have a home game against Fulham as they look to end a three-match losing run. Bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace travel to Coventry, whilst Chelsea welcome Leeds to Stamford Bridge. Elsewhere, in-form Bournemouth host Nottingham Forest, Aston Villa take on Sunderland, and Ipswich make the trip to Spurs. Presented by Gabby Logan, with Joe Hart and Alan Shearer.

programme.title: Far from the Madding Crowd
programme.desc: Beautiful and headstrong Bathsheba Everdene catches the eye of local farmer Gabriel Oak when she arrives to live with her aunt in the Dorset village of Norcombe. She declines his offer of marriage, but their lives continue to intertwine as fate brings contrasting fortunes to both of them. Adapted by David Nicholls for BBC Films from the novel by Thomas Hardy.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Will it be game, set and match for Ben Cooper’s or Kate Bliss’s team on this episode? In Box, near Bath, presenter Caroline Hawley visits the UK’s only tennis ball manufacturer, where she learns about the origins of the tennis ball and how it gets its all-important bounce! Hoping to ace it at the fair are friends Helen and Marsha on the red team. Their opponents in blue are pals Clark and Michele, who are in it ‘for gavels and fame’. With 60 minutes on the clock, they take a shine to a Georgian-style silver serving dish – but not the three-figure price tag! The reds’ first stop is a striking pair of arts and crafts copper candlesticks, but the cost quickly snuffs out their interest in them. At Tim Weeks’s auction in Wiltshire, the bidders snap up the teams’ items. Will it come down to a battle of the bonus buys?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The cryptocurrency scammers based in Albania are back at it as the team listen in. This group claim to help their victims recover lost investments, but in reality, they are just looking to steal more money. With efforts to get through on the phone failing, the ground team are dispatched to try to prevent a woman from Woking paying out, but local roadworks throw a spanner into the plan. As the scam nears its conclusion, Nick and Harleen watch on helplessly as ground interceptors Meea and Harriet do their utmost to beat the traffic and reach the woman in time. The team also join forces with ethical hacker Dan to investigate and confront a man from Cameroon claiming to sell horses on social media.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

The reds’ first stop is a striking pair of arts and crafts copper candlesticks, but the cost quickly snuffs out their interest in them. At Tim Weeks’s auction in Wiltshire, the bidders snap up the teams’ items. Will it come down to a battle of the bonus buys?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The cryptocurrency scammers based in Albania are back at it as the team listen in. This group claim to help their victims recover lost investments, but in reality, they are just looking to steal more money. With efforts to get through on the phone failing, the ground team are dispatched to try to prevent a woman from Woking paying out, but local roadworks throw a spanner into the plan. As the scam nears its conclusion, Nick and Harleen watch on helplessly as ground interceptors Meea and Harriet do their utmost to beat the traffic and reach the woman in time. The team also join forces with ethical hacker Dan to investigate and confront a man from Cameroon claiming to sell horses on social media.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives

And Matt speaks to a man who chased down a gang of suspected car thieves all by himself.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: The worlds of windsurfing and funeral directing collide when a body is found washed up on the beach. With Joe along for the ride, Rose and Raj must find what connects them.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Three generations of the same family need help from Jules Hudson to find them a new, rural Norfolk home. In the kitty is £800,000 for a four-bedroom house, an annexe for Granny and enough land for a Shetland pony. Jules also needs a keen eye to spot some of the world’s rarest (and camera-shy) species of deer and antelope at a local safari park.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

With music from Take That, performing their current single, Higher.

programme.title: Zooport
programme.desc: When a scandal hits BAFTA-winning film-maker Dav, he returns to his home town of Newport in a bid to rescue his career. Instead, he is plunged into a whirlwind of past mistakes: unresolved history with an ex, a volatile reunion with his former best friend, and a bizarre new home life with a brooding Ukrainian refugee and Dav’s extremely available mother.

programme.title: Fall
programme.desc: A fast drop and a sudden stop await Becky (Grace Fulton) and Hunter (Virginia Gardner) as they find themselves trapped 2,000 feet up an abandoned radio tower in the desert. Highly trained and resourceful, these climbers marking the tragic passing of a friend were not ready for every eventuality. A series of unfortunate events see their gear and supplies taken from them, and as temperatures rise and vultures begin to circle, the chance of survival begins to fall rapidly. A heart-pounding tale of survival from the producers of 47 Meters Down, where sacrifice may just be the only way out.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Surrey, Sarah Moore is at Witley recycling centre, trawling the car boots in the hope of finding some potential gems in need of creative magic. Upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence are tested by a wooden cabinet in disrepair, four chairs in a mix of styles get a radical revamp from woodworker Martin Hough, whilst Sarah must think out of the box when she takes on a metal trunk full of vintage tools.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing

The show begins with a group performance from the entire cast and the legendary Basement Jaxx. Then, Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome our couples to the world-famous ballroom for their biggest performances of the competition. Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke have packed their paddles and will be sharing expert advice before the vote opens and you have your say. Which couple’s performance will be the talk of the tower?

programme.title: Honey

Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

Elsewhere, in-form Bournemouth host Nottingham Forest, Aston Villa take on Sunderland, and Ipswich make the trip to Spurs. Presented by Gabby Logan, with Joe Hart and Alan Shearer.

Adapted by David Nicholls for BBC Films from the novel by Thomas Hardy.

programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: The Graham Norton Show

With music from Take That, performing their current single, Higher.

programme.title: Zooport
programme.desc: When a scandal hits BAFTA-winning film-maker Dav, he returns to his home town of Newport in a bid to rescue his career. Instead, he is plunged into a whirlwind of past mistakes: unresolved history with an ex, a volatile reunion with his former best friend, and a bizarre new home life with a brooding Ukrainian refugee and Dav’s extremely available mother.

programme.title: Fall
programme.desc: A fast drop and a sudden stop await Becky (Grace Fulton) and Hunter (Virginia Gardner) as they find themselves trapped 2,000 feet up an abandoned radio tower in the desert. Highly trained and resourceful, these climbers marking the tragic passing of a friend were not ready for every eventuality. A series of unfortunate events see their gear and supplies taken from them, and as temperatures rise and vultures begin to circle, the chance of survival begins to fall rapidly. A heart-pounding tale of survival from the producers of 47 Meters Down, where sacrifice may just be the only way out.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

Adapted by David Nicholls for BBC Films from the novel by Thomas Hardy.

An insurer questions a whiplash claim after a barely visible bump, while a horse rider films an overtake that nearly ends in a head-on crash. A van runs a red light, but tracing the driver brings an unexpected twist.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A newbie Derbyshire developer admits he's winging it! In Bournemouth, Martin is gobsmacked by the building he's in. Jacqui is in a Norfolk village called Little Snoring, but there's no time for her to take a nap with a property to see.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Will it be game, set and match for Ben Cooper’s or Kate Bliss’s team on this episode? In Box, near Bath, presenter Caroline Hawley visits the UK’s only tennis ball manufacturer, where she learns about the origins of the tennis ball and how it gets its all-important bounce! Hoping to ace it at the fair are friends Helen and Marsha on the red team. Their opponents in blue are pals Clark and Michele, who are in it ‘for gavels and fame’. With 60 minutes on the clock, they take a shine to a Georgian-style silver serving dish – but not the three-figure price tag! The reds’ first stop is a striking pair of arts and crafts copper candlesticks, but the cost quickly snuffs out their interest in them. At Tim Weeks’s auction in Wiltshire, the bidders snap up the teams’ items. Will it come down to a battle of the bonus buys?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The cryptocurrency scammers based in Albania are back at it as the team listen in. This group claim to help their victims recover lost investments, but in reality, they are just looking to steal more money. With efforts to get through on the phone failing, the ground team are dispatched to try to prevent a woman from Woking paying out, but local roadworks throw a spanner into the plan. As the scam nears its conclusion, Nick and Harleen watch on helplessly as ground interceptors Meea and Harriet do their utmost to beat the traffic and reach the woman in time. The team also join forces with ethical hacker Dan to investigate and confront a man from Cameroon claiming to sell horses on social media.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When a group of odd-job workmen turn up at Linda’s 87-year-old father's house saying he needs work doing, she races over before he parts with potentially hundreds of pounds. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gets his hands dirty as he shows how our rubbish can be a treasure trove for criminals. And Matt speaks to a man who chased down a gang of suspected car thieves all by himself.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: It’s sea breezes and fresh starts in Devon as Nicki Chapman helps retirees from Northamptonshire find their perfect coastal retreat. They’re dreaming of a single-storey home close to the sea, and one of the properties delivers breathtaking ocean views right from the terrace. Nicki also meets a couple raising a family in a Dartmoor village, who share their love of the outdoors by mapping walks in the National Park for all ages and abilities to enjoy.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Dom and plaster expert Rich try to preserve some World War II Polish art before it is lost forever. Meanwhile, David Burville repairs a clockwork ship, and Will gets to grips with shinty.

The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: The worlds of windsurfing and funeral directing collide when a body is found washed up on the beach. With Joe along for the ride, Rose and Raj must find what connects them.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Three generations of the same family need help from Jules Hudson to find them a new, rural Norfolk home. In the kitty is £800,000 for a four-bedroom house, an annexe for Granny and enough land for a Shetland pony. Jules also needs a keen eye to spot some of the world’s rarest (and camera-shy) species of deer and antelope at a local safari park.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

Adapted by David Nicholls for BBC Films from the novel by Thomas Hardy.

programme.desc: Cyclist James Taylor's ride home in Bristol turns terrifying when a driver follows dangerously close, then squeezes past. His cameras capture the angry confrontation. An insurer questions a whiplash claim after a barely visible bump, while a horse rider films an overtake that nearly ends in a head-on crash. A van runs a red light, but tracing the driver brings an unexpected twist.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A newbie Derbyshire developer admits he's winging it! In Bournemouth, Martin is gobsmacked by the building he's in. Jacqui is in a Norfolk village called Little Snoring, but there's no time for her to take a nap with a property to see.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Will it be game, set and match for Ben Cooper’s or Kate Bliss’s team on this episode? In Box, near Bath, presenter Caroline Hawley visits the UK’s only tennis ball manufacturer, where she learns about the origins of the tennis ball and how it gets its all-important bounce! Hoping to ace it at the fair are friends Helen and Marsha on the red team. Their opponents in blue are pals Clark and Michele, who are in it ‘for gavels and fame’. With 60 minutes on the clock, they take a shine to a Georgian-style silver serving dish – but not the three-figure price tag! The reds’ first stop is a striking pair of arts and crafts copper candlesticks, but the cost quickly snuffs out their interest in them. At Tim Weeks’s auction in Wiltshire, the bidders snap up the teams’ items. Will it come down to a battle of the bonus buys?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The cryptocurrency scammers based in Albania are back at it as the team listen in. This group claim to help their victims recover lost investments, but in reality, they are just looking to steal more money. With efforts to get through on the phone failing, the ground team are dispatched to try to prevent a woman from Woking paying out, but local roadworks throw a spanner into the plan. As the scam nears its conclusion, Nick and Harleen watch on helplessly as ground interceptors Meea and Harriet do their utmost to beat the traffic and reach the woman in time. The team also join forces with ethical hacker Dan to investigate and confront a man from Cameroon claiming to sell horses on social media.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When a group of odd-job workmen turn up at Linda’s 87-year-old father's house saying he needs work doing, she races over before he parts with potentially hundreds of pounds. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gets his hands dirty as he shows how our rubbish can be a treasure trove for criminals. And Matt speaks to a man who chased down a gang of suspected car thieves all by himself.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: It’s sea breezes and fresh starts in Devon as Nicki Chapman helps retirees from Northamptonshire find their perfect coastal retreat. They’re dreaming of a single-storey home close to the sea, and one of the properties delivers breathtaking ocean views right from the terrace. Nicki also meets a couple raising a family in a Dartmoor village, who share their love of the outdoors by mapping walks in the National Park for all ages and abilities to enjoy.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Dom and plaster expert Rich try to preserve some World War II Polish art before it is lost forever. Meanwhile, David Burville repairs a clockwork ship, and Will gets to grips with shinty.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – Lee, Has, Nina, Rob and Amanda – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: The worlds of windsurfing and funeral directing collide when a body is found washed up on the beach. With Joe along for the ride, Rose and Raj must find what connects them.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Three generations of the same family need help from Jules Hudson to find them a new, rural Norfolk home. In the kitty is £800,000 for a four-bedroom house, an annexe for Granny and enough land for a Shetland pony. Jules also needs a keen eye to spot some of the world’s rarest (and camera-shy) species of deer and antelope at a local safari park.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – William, Nicky, Abz, Chris and Charlotte – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: BBC Children in Need
programme.desc: Owain Wyn Evans’s Four Nations Challenge for Children in Need.

programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: The Graham Norton Show
programme.desc: Together on Graham's sofa are Hollywood legend Robert De Niro and comedy great Ben Stiller, reunited in Focker-in-Law; Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh, talking about her new TV series Bladerunner 2099; and top chef Jamie Oliver, whose latest book is 20-Minute Meals. With music from Take That, performing their current single, Higher.

programme.title: Fall
programme.desc: A fast drop and a sudden stop await Becky (Grace Fulton) and Hunter (Virginia Gardner) as they find themselves trapped 2,000 feet up an abandoned radio tower in the desert. Highly trained and resourceful, these climbers marking the tragic passing of a friend were not ready for every eventuality. A series of unfortunate events see their gear and supplies taken from them, and as temperatures rise and vultures begin to circle, the chance of survival begins to fall rapidly. A heart-pounding tale of survival from the producers of 47 Meters Down, where sacrifice may just be the only way out.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Surrey, Sarah Moore is at Witley recycling centre, trawling the car boots in the hope of finding some potential gems in need of creative magic. Upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence are tested by a wooden cabinet in disrepair, four chairs in a mix of styles get a radical revamp from woodworker Martin Hough, whilst Sarah must think out of the box when she takes on a metal trunk full of vintage tools.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A creative couple from London want to leave city life behind in search of new adventures in Gloucestershire, and Chris Bavin is on hand to guide them. Along with presenting a lovely selection of houses, Chris also visits a local football club to check out for himself why it’s green by name and green by nature.

programme.title: Final Score

programme.title: The Famous Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene. Five celebrities, Maisie Adam, JJ Chalmers, Harry Clark, Abby Cook and Colin Jackson, race in moving podiums across a star-spangled themed studio to try to win £10,000 for their chosen charity.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s that time of year again – Strictly returns to the home of ballroom dancing, the iconic Blackpool Tower, for a spectacular night of dancing. The show begins with a group performance from the entire cast and the legendary Basement Jaxx. Then, Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome our couples to the world-famous ballroom for their biggest performances of the competition. Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke have packed their paddles and will be sharing expert advice before the vote opens and you have your say. Which couple’s performance will be the talk of the tower?

programme.title: Michael McIntyre's The Wheel
programme.desc: Michael McIntyre hosts his hit game show packed with huge stars, big laughs and a giant spinning wheel. Can the contestants answer their way to a fortune? The celebrity experts in this episode are Italian Bach, Kerry Godliman, Trevor Nelson, Angela Scanlon, Alex Scott, Josh Widdicombe, Bez and Shaun Ryder.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Friedrich is ordered by his boss Schimmel to ramp up his efforts to locate Greta, believing she is the key to the Hermann Metzl case. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: The worlds of windsurfing and funeral directing collide when a body is found washed up on the beach. With Joe along for the ride, Rose and Raj must find what connects them.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Three generations of the same family need help from Jules Hudson to find them a new, rural Norfolk home. In the kitty is £800,000 for a four-bedroom house, an annexe for Granny and enough land for a Shetland pony. Jules also needs a keen eye to spot some of the world’s rarest (and camera-shy) species of deer and antelope at a local safari park.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

With music from Take That, performing their current single, Higher.

programme.title: Fall
programme.desc: A fast drop and a sudden stop await Becky (Grace Fulton) and Hunter (Virginia Gardner) as they find themselves trapped 2,000 feet up an abandoned radio tower in the desert. Highly trained and resourceful, these climbers marking the tragic passing of a friend were not ready for every eventuality. A series of unfortunate events see their gear and supplies taken from them, and as temperatures rise and vultures begin to circle, the chance of survival begins to fall rapidly. A heart-pounding tale of survival from the producers of 47 Meters Down, where sacrifice may just be the only way out.
