programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

Hoping to ace it at the fair are friends Helen and Marsha on the red team. Their opponents in blue are pals Clark and Michele, who are in it ‘for gavels and fame’. With 60 minutes on the clock, they take a shine to a Georgian-style silver serving dish – but not the three-figure price tag! The reds’ first stop is a striking pair of arts and crafts copper candlesticks, but the cost quickly snuffs out their interest in them. At Tim Weeks’s auction in Wiltshire, the bidders snap up the teams’ items. Will it come down to a battle of the bonus buys?

This group claim to help their victims recover lost investments, but in reality, they are just looking to steal more money. With efforts to get through on the phone failing, the ground team are dispatched to try to prevent a woman from Woking paying out, but local roadworks throw a spanner into the plan. As the scam nears its conclusion, Nick and Harleen watch on helplessly as ground interceptors Meea and Harriet do their utmost to beat the traffic and reach the woman in time. The team also join forces with ethical hacker Dan to investigate and confront a man from Cameroon claiming to sell horses on social media.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Three generations of the same family need help from Jules Hudson to find them a new, rural Norfolk home. In the kitty is £800,000 for a four-bedroom house, an annexe for Granny and enough land for a Shetland pony. Jules also needs a keen eye to spot some of the world’s rarest (and camera-shy) species of deer and antelope at a local safari park.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: Fall
programme.desc: A fast drop and a sudden stop await Becky (Grace Fulton) and Hunter (Virginia Gardner) as they find themselves trapped 2,000 feet up an abandoned radio tower in the desert. Highly trained and resourceful, these climbers marking the tragic passing of a friend were not ready for every eventuality. A series of unfortunate events see their gear and supplies taken from them, and as temperatures rise and vultures begin to circle, the chance of survival begins to fall rapidly. A heart-pounding tale of survival from the producers of 47 Meters Down, where sacrifice may just be the only way out.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Wild Cameramen at Work
programme.desc: Five of the best wildlife cameramen in the world have their roots in Scotland: Doug Allan, Gordon Buchanan and Doug Anderson were all born north of the border, while John Aitchison and Mark Smith have chosen to make Scotland their home. In this stunning series they revisit some of their favourite natural history moments from their global careers, and tell us how Scotland has helped them hone their specialist skills for capturing some of the greatest images to grace our television screens. Narrated by David Attenborough - the first episode of this stunning new series reveals the hardships and hazards involved when filming wildlife in the world's most extreme environments - the Arctic and Antarctic. Legendary polar cameraman and diver Doug Allan relives some of his most hair-raising encounters and returns to the place where his underwater career began - the freezing depths of a Highland river.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Jean Johansson is at Beechgrove, which has had a Christmas-style makeover. As part of a series helping families get ready for a fabulous Christmas, there are ideas to get your kids creating and crafting. Plus ways to make handmade presents, fabulous food and drink tips and gift suggestions, along with the usual top gardening advice from the Beechgrove team. In this episode, it’s all about the decorations. If you are about to choose a tree, just what should you be looking for? Once you’ve got one, there is expert advice on how to light and decorate it. And if you want a break from Christmas preparation, Carole Baxter will have advice on the garden jobs to be done right now.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: A special episode from north Sutherland at the top of the Scottish mainland. Dougie steps out into the Flow Country, a vast expanse of blanket peat bog, where he charts the changes in its land use and its recent designation as a Unesco World Heritage site. Arlene catches up with sheep farmer Joyce Campbell to see how she has made the switch from traditional hill farming to regenerative agriculture. Arlene also visits Strath Halladale, where she meets a man who gave up city life to run the family croft 37 years ago. She finds out how he has built a thriving timber business and brought jobs to the area. And at Loch Hope, Leanna meets the biologists working to protect precious sea trout populations.

programme.title: Hamza's Hidden Wild Isles
programme.desc: Wonder is everywhere – if you know where to look. From sunny beaches to rugged moors, craggy munros to city streets, Hamza Yassin reveals amazing wildlife hidden around the UK. The limited edition booklet is no longer available to order, but you can download a version from the Open University’s website.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: The Chief kicks-off his rugby-themed anti-crime campaign with the help of Scotland legend Gavin Hasting, while traffic cops Singh and McKirdy expertly utilise a dinosaur grabber in the name of socially distanced policing. Call responder Maggie Le Beau is well versed in the rudest place names on the map, and rural reorganisation has repercussions for the key partnership of McIntosh and Mackay.

programme.title: The Chief
programme.desc: Who better to record the audiobook of the autobiography of Scotland's greatest policeman than tartan Hollywood legend Dougray Scott? The work is entitled No Apologies, and the Chief is a stickler for detail. He is soon coaching Scott's performance on everything from historical case accuracy to sexiness. Will a tight deadline and the crime-fighting needs of a nation prevent the Chief achieving lyrical literary perfection? This is the story of the recording of the story of the making of the main man - Chief Commissioner Cameron Miekelson.

programme.title: Make It to Munich
programme.desc: Documentary following Ethan Walker, a promising teenage footballer from Aberdeenshire who suffered life-threatening injuries in a road traffic accident just months into a football scholarship at a US university. Aided in his recovery by pioneering Scottish surgeon (and former footballer) Professor Gordon Mackay, Ethan undertakes a charity cycle ride from Glasgow to Munich for Scotland’s opening match against Germany in Euro 2024, just nine months after his accident. Entrusted by the Scottish national team to carry the match pennant on his back for the whole journey and deliver it in time for kick-off, Ethan is accompanied by Gordon, Tartan Army foot-soldier Stephen Collie and film-maker Martyn Robertson.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police investigate the disappearance of a young monk from a monastery on a remote private island in Orkney. The mystery deepens when there appears to be no evidence of how he could have left the island. In Aviemore, a rock festival erupts into violence. In Inverness, officers hunt a man after a woman is attacked in a cemetery, while campers in Fort William take a wrong turn.

programme.desc: When a family home in an affluent suburb of Glasgow is deliberately set on fire, detectives race to determine who attacked the young couple staying there and why.

programme.title: Men of the Manosphere
programme.desc: James Blake joins three young men to explore why they’ve turned to the so-called manosphere to achieve success, and how it’s influenced their real lives.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Cardiff-based hopeless romantic Lewis just can’t help hearing wedding bells and talking through future life plans on date one, but that’s not the only obstacle to him getting a second date. If he’s not ranting about his exes, he’s zoning out mid-conversation, leaving his dates lost for words and never calling them again. Tired of listening to yet another of his first-date failures, Lewis’s best mate Megan thinks it’s time for an intervention, so she enlists the help one of Gen Z’s sassiest sex and relationships experts, Oloni, to drop some hard home truths on 20-year-old Lewis to try to end the bad habits that send his dates running for the hills. Oloni gives Lewis a reality check as his friends and exes tell it how it is via video feedback, explaining where it’s all going wrong. Oloni and Megan watch on as Lewis goes on a series of first dates that will challenge him to rethink his dating behaviour and become a better dater. Can Lewis ditch the wedding planning, stop raking up stories about his exes and focus on the conversation long enough to prove he can be a good date?

programme.title: Movies with Ali Plumb
programme.desc: BBC Radio 1 film critic Ali Plumb explores the UK’s most iconic and unexpected film locations. Ali provides film lovers with a guide to this film location nation, stepping into the scenes themselves to bring the magic to life, In this episode, Ali travels through the silver screen sights of Liverpool.

programme.title: Top Gear

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Sports mockumentary about GB Paralympian Darren Silverstone, who stole the hearts of a nation before his infamous chokey-o in Tokyo. For the first time, he tells his story - and starts his glorious comeback. In Tokyo 2020, Darren Silverstone was the Paras GB poster boy. (He was on yoghurts, too.) He cruised to the final and charmed the nation along the way with his signature dance move, the dazzle. But as he took that final bend ready to take gold, Silverstone lost his head and celebrated too soon - and in the process, became a national figure of fun. His subsequent journey in the public eye brought approval and consternation in equal measure: from those unforgettably self-deprecating betting adverts to his turn on The Masked Singer as Breadbin. Darren’s best friend and pilot rider in Tokyo, little Paul Potter, was never seen again in the public eye. The two haven’t spoken since. And now, Silverstone’s back. Ready to take to the tandem at Paris 2024. But is he ready? Who will he be riding with? This is I Am Darren.

programme.title: Nativity!
programme.desc: Paul Maddens is charged with the biggest challenge of his life - mounting his primary school's musical version of the Nativity. Competing against the posh neighbouring school for the honour of the best-reviewed show in town, the stakes are raised when Paul idly boasts that his ex-girlfriend Jennifer, a Hollywood producer, is coming to see his show with a view to turning it into a film. The only trouble is - they haven't spoken in years... Comedy from BBC Films.

As part of its commitment to community theatre, the BBC has commissioned The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society, an amateur dramatics group, to recreate the JM Barrie classic as part of their festive programming. But can they pull it off? Narrated by David Suchet and filmed in front of a live audience, watch as Peter Pan flies through the air, Captain Hook and his pirates set adrift in the lagoon, and Tinkerbell is due to light up the stage in a stunning electrical costume... what can possibly go wrong?! With their trademark comic mayhem, expect hilarious stunts, chaos, technical hitches, flying mishaps and cast disputes on the way to Neverland with hilarious and disastrous results.

He cruised to the final and charmed the nation along the way with his signature dance move, the dazzle. Despite the grapes being grown just a few metres away, these reds are a class apart.

programme.desc: Weasy falls in love with a gold watch, but it belongs to the farmer...

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Mr Friendlyface is acting very strangely indeed. He refuses to stamp any of Admin Bunny’s documents, keeps getting distracted by butterflies, and seems oddly happy! The heroes are extremely suspicious and decide that someone must have swapped him with a doppelganger. Now they must quest to find out where the real Friendlyface is and get him back before the forest descends into total chaos.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings lay hands on an ancient console, and Grizzy is transported into the game.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck and Frog are working at a supermarket alongside Toad and Flamingo, who keep ruining Duck and Frog's hard work to make them look bad. Why are they being so mean?

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Roy, Crocalor and Kilowattrel take on Drayton in a spirited rematch.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: The Winx indulge in a day of fun at the amusement park in Magixia but are suddenly attacked by Vexius. This time, however, they may be able to stop him with the help of unexpected allies...

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Meet new BP presenter Leo, who takes to the skies in an incredible skydive challenge to earn his Blue Peter Badge - can he achieve a world record on his very first show?

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall heads to Oman, where he abseils to a verreaux's eagle nest, tracks down wolves and swims alongside a super pod made up of over 100 dolphins.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty celebrates the rewards of winter gardening - sharing ideas, inspiration and timely jobs to keep gardeners busy now, while reminding us that warmer days lie ahead. At Longmeadow, he has hellebores to plant, peas to sow and practical advice on propagating roses. Sue Kent gets to work on her allotment, where there’s always plenty to do during the colder months, including some clever composting. Jamie Butterworth takes a tour of one of Somerset’s most imaginative topiary gardens. In Belfast, a local community tells the tale of how their once neglected alleyway has become their pride and joy. Carol Klein unearths some radical new thinking on how flowers may be adapting to climate change, while Rekha Mistry travels to RHS Garden Bridgewater to see how garden varieties of tomato and mint are put to the test.

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham is joined by Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin for another lively, curiosity-fuelled adventure into the wonders of Britain’s wildlife, uncovering nature’s most fascinating secrets and surprising stories. This week, the team dives into some intriguing autumn mysteries: why don’t seals drown? What is the UK’s most deadly mushroom? And what extraordinary creature has the power to keep autumn leaves alive? Expect surprising discoveries, weird and wonderful wildlife facts and plenty of questions along the way!

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: Anita Rani pays a Christmas visit to Baroness Floella Benjamin, a pivotal figure to generations of young TV viewers. Born in Trinidad and Tobago, Floella arrived in London at the age of ten as part of the Windrush generation. Together, they retrace that journey and reflect on Dame Floella's extraordinary life shaped by faith and the festive season: from stage actor and iconic Play School presenter to businesswoman, child rights campaigner, dame and baroness, and even playing a role in King Charles III's coronation.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing's Tales from a Kitchen Garden
programme.desc: Marcus plans to bring in some ducks, but things aren’t as simple as they seem as he heads out onto the lake to create a new home for them. Heading to Devon, he discovers the perfect breed for the smallholding and picks up some top tips and tricks on how to rear them. Back on the farm, the bounty of the kitchen garden inspires a visit to a local community fridge to learn more about how it works, before a neighbour pops over to give him a lesson on what is edible and growing wild in the hedgerows and bushes that surround the smallholding. Once the new ducks arrive and are safely in their new home, he cooks up a fantastic feast inspired by a British classic, the ploughman's lunch.

programme.title: Nadiya’s Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Nadiya shows off her easy celebration bakes, which range from a glittering meringue layer cake to a slow-cooked lamb curry fit for a feast, with an American-inspired seafood extravaganza.

programme.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
programme.desc: Screen adaptation of Oscar Wilde's celebrated play in which two Victorian gentlemen both adopt a double identity under the name of Ernest and end up in trouble when they both turn up at the same country house one weekend.

programme.title: Strangers on a Train
programme.desc: Alfred Hitchcock's suspense classic about two men who plot a perfect murder. When tennis pro Guy Haines meets smooth-talking Bruno Antony in the bar of a train, he finds the stranger sympathetic with his desire to be rid of his clinging wife. The sinister Bruno then proposes that they swap murders: Bruno will murder Guy's wife, and Guy will do away with Bruno's father. From Patricia Highsmith's novel.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The programme comes from the Platform in Morecambe, Lancashire, which in its day was the main station bringing holidaymakers to the town. Antiques experts Charles Hanson and Catherine Southon find treasures to take to auction, including a vintage Rolex watch. Paul Martin discovers the rags-to-riches story of the town's most famous son - Eric Morecambe.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Broadcasting legend Bob Harris and queen of motor sports Suzi Perry burn rubber across south east England in a racy 1974 Ford Escort RS 2000. But can they flip antiques for profit? Steering them in the right direction are doyens Margie Cooper and Raj Bisram, both veteran road trippers and rivals to the core. What starts out as a hunt for music and travel collectibles changes tack very early on. Bob falls for a pair of romantic champagne flutes in a love heart stand, while Suzy steps back in time when she discovers a Japanese glass fishing float. Along the way, they learn to raise their profile through the art of silhouette portraiture, with some amazing results. But at the auction, there can be only one winner. Will Bob reach the number one spot, or will Suzy be racing for the stars?

programme.title: The Eagle Has Landed
programme.desc: All-action World War II adventure. On the morning of 6 November 1943, the military authorities in Berlin receive a simple message - 'The Eagle Has Landed'. In a daring kidnap attempt, a small force of crack German paratroopers are poised to snatch Winston Churchill and return with him to Germany. If they succeed in their mission, it could alter the course of the war. Who can stop them?

programme.title: 40 Hidden Music Treasures at the BBC
programme.desc: A collection of 40 rarely seen musical moments that don't often get to escape from the BBC vaults. Featuring Roachford on The Roland Rat Show, David Bowie on Friday Night with Jonathan Ross, Mary J Blige appearing on Davina McCall's chat show and one of Gloria Estefan's several star turns on the Royal Variety Show over the years.

programme.title: 40 Hidden Music Treasures at the BBC
programme.desc: Another deep dive into the BBC’s music archives, where the musical map is pointed away from Top of the Pops on a quest to uncover 40 rarely seen performances and hidden gems. Featuring Bronski Beat’s first BBC performance of Smalltown Boy, Rihanna’s rockier version of Umbrella, Sophie Ellis-Bextor covering Pulp’s Do You Remember the First Time? and Kate Bush pairing up for a tango during Hounds of Love. These tucked-away treats and many, many more make this a journey that musical fans are certain to treasure.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear explores wellbeing and what it means to live a healthy, balanced life. Presenter Marios Costi shares practical advice on reducing stress, finding calm and making positive changes while meeting inspiring deaf people who are breaking down barriers, building confidence and pursuing their dreams. Marios talks with Avril Langard-Tang, a senior lecturer at the University of Wolverhampton and the first deaf woman to walk solo from John O’Groats to Land’s End. She reflects on her extraordinary 980-mile journey, the physical and emotional challenges she faced and the support she received from the deaf community along the way.

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk’s groundbreaking history of cinema begins. Cunk meets Hollywood legends and interrogates the writer of Die Hard, as she starts her quest deep, deep into cinema. She witnesses the shockingly poor picture quality of the earliest films and marvels at the beards of their Victorian inventors; she gasps audibly at the invention of sound; and she critiques some of the supposedly finest creations of Hollywood’s Golden Age. Along the way she interviews filmmakers, actors and critics, including several you’ve definitely heard of, and she (and you) finally discovers the true meaning of The Wizard of Oz.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: For a live demonstration of terroir, Eva heads to Domaine Dujac, home of the current most-wanted Burgundy wine. Standing on one side of a road, owner Jeremy Seysses points to a parcel of grand cru (the very best) of Clos de la Roche. On the other side is a premier cru (the next best) - a Gevrey-Chambertin Combottes. Back at the winery, Eva tucks into beef cheeks bathed in Domaine Dujac for a classic boeuf bourguignon lunch. Despite the grapes being grown just a few metres away, these reds are a class apart.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Siobhan, her partner Timmie and their two young children hope to bring new life to their small village in Ireland by renovating the old post office to become their forever home. But with funds running low and work grinding to a halt, will their dream family home become a reality?

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear joins BBC Children in Need for a special programme exploring the difference funding makes to the lives of deaf and disabled children, and their families. Featuring inspiring personal stories, a fun lip-reading challenge and the incredible people and organisations helping children build confidence, find friendship and feel they belong. Select ‘sign language’ to watch a version of this programme on iPlayer without the voice over.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family and friends Frankie, James, Susanne and Jason – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Colin Murray and Edith Bowman explore St George’s Market in Belfast and meet a social media sensation who reveals the secrets of healthy and inexpensive one-pot meals. Farmer Jim Smith discovers how one farm is turning its oats into milk, food journalist Leyla Kazim is in Norfolk to find out the secrets of producing mustard, and farmer Meinir Howells reveals just why Welsh lamb is so popular.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's coastal railway journey takes him past lochs and castles on the Far North Line to Britain’s northernmost railway station at Thurso.

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: Karen of Ladram hunts for hake off Cornwall, a rookie crew work in the Irish Sea, trainee skipper Michael steps up in a storm, and Tydus heads out in search of crabs in the North Sea.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team are in Lancaster, where items uncovered include a valuable pair of clogs, a moving series of letters from the Crimea, an anti-slavery ring and a rare and intricately woven tapestry.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Longleat in Wiltshire, home to the seventh Marquess of Bath, where a wide variety of antiques and collectibles are put before experts Claire Rawle and Michael Baggott at the valuation tables, including a stunning amethyst and pearl brooch. But it's an autograph album with a set of Beatles signatures that has the experts guessing. Are they genuine or not? All is revealed at the auction. Paul Martin also takes a trip to London to unearth the hidden architectural gems of one of Wiltshire's most famous sons - Sir Christopher Wren.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jake Bhardwaj, Sue Cleaver, Rachel Parris and Rav Wilding take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is back with the latest news and behind-the-scenes action from the world of Strictly. Also, costume designer Vicky Gill has an exclusive look at what the couples will be wearing in Blackpool's Tower Ballroom.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sonali Shah showcases some superb Somerset properties to a couple who have a budget of £700,000 and want a countryside home where they can upgrade an allotment to their very own back garden veggie patch. Sonali also learns about the potentially perilous Bristol Channel and meets the volunteers who operate two life-saving rescue hovercrafts.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police investigate the disappearance of a young monk from a monastery on a remote private island in Orkney. The mystery deepens when there appears to be no evidence of how he could have left the island. In Aviemore, a rock festival erupts into violence. In Inverness, officers hunt a man after a woman is attacked in a cemetery, while campers in Fort William take a wrong turn.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: By the start of the new millennium, the three chefs had changed British dining forever. This episode follows what happens when the rivalry that made them gets harder to walk away from than to feed, and brings them together for the first time in decades, exploring how each man handled the success he had fought for. Will time have healed old wounds, or will old rivalries still burn brightly?

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk continues her epic journey deep, deep into film. She interrogates some of the world’s foremost filmmakers and critics, discovers an age of screen icons, from Marilyn Monroe to Wayne John, learns how Hollywood movies changed as American social values relaxed, and discovers how, believe it or not, other countries were making films as well. Along the way, she gives her verdict on classics like Jaws, Taxi Driver, and Citizen Ken - very much the Citizen Kane of films about people called Ken.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O’Connell.

programme.title: Past Lives
programme.desc: Following two childhood friends over the course of 24 years while they contemplate the nature of their relationship as they grow apart, living different lives.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear joins BBC Children in Need for a special programme exploring the difference funding makes to the lives of deaf and disabled children, and their families. Featuring inspiring personal stories, a fun lip-reading challenge and the incredible people and organisations helping children build confidence, find friendship and feel they belong. Select ‘sign language’ to watch a version of this programme on iPlayer without the voice over.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: The standout chefs from the week’s heats battle it out again in the quarter-final. The stakes are higher, the challenges more demanding, and the judges’ expectations are greater than ever.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Irish film star Chris O'Dowd joins Bill Murray and his friend Tom Coyne for a lively round of golf, with enthusiasm occasionally outstripping ability. Away from the fairways, a traditional rambling house takes Bill outside his comfort zone as he explores Ireland's rich storytelling traditions. Later, in a packed Irish pub, the music starts – and staying on the sidelines proves impossible.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A newbie Derbyshire developer admits he's winging it! In Bournemouth, Martin is gobsmacked by the building he's in. Jacqui is in a Norfolk village called Little Snoring, but there's no time for her to take a nap with a property to see.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Briony May Williams helps discerning house hunters from a town in Kent relocate to the quieter countryside of Norfolk and Suffolk. With three dogs and an impressive collection of cars and motorcycles, there’s plenty to accommodate. So, finding a home that’s not too big, not too small, but just right proves quite the challenge. Briony also pulls on her waders in the River Waveney to discover what’s being done to keep its waters clean for wild swimmers.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul are in County Durham, fishing the River Tees for a rare species of wild brown trout. Bob takes Paul on a trip across the landscapes of his youth, navigating the area through the lens of his six-year-old self. Bob lost his dad when he was very young, but some of the memories he holds dear are of the fishing trips they used to go on. Later, Bob invites their old friend Reece Shearsmith to dinner. Reece has some particularly spooky local tales to tell them about the River Tees.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: With the promise of unimaginable computing power, a global race for quantum supremacy is raging. Hannah Fry looks inside the IBM research facility, one of the oldest tech companies in the world, to uncover the future of quantum technology. She explores the unprecedented potential of quantum computing and how precarious this advanced power may be in the wrong hands. Through her exclusive interviews with world-class experts in quantum technologies, Hannah explores the international quantum arms race between the US and China. She breaks down the implications of this 21st-century race and how a quantum future could change the very nature of humanity.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: The European Union's foreign policy chief sits down with Nick in Brussels to discuss her uncompromising stance on Russia, Europe's future relationship with the UK and how her Estonian family's experience under Soviet rule formed her worldview as Europe's top diplomat.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, four colleagues from Colchester Zoo, Lizzie, Kez, Mo and Sue – take on the Bridge of Lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher explores the annual Neath food festival and finds out whether traditional or exotic Welsh cakes are more popular among the visitors. Food journalist Leyla Kazim reveals secrets of tomato growing on a large and small scale, while farmer Jim Smith gets stuck into making marmalade. Ryan Hand tries an experiment to find out whether there is such a thing as ‘brain food’.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael crosses over to the Orkney Islands, visiting the former naval base at Scapa Flow and learning about the islands' extensive Norwegian connections.

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: Margaret of Ladram gambles in the Bristol Channel, Emilia Jayne chases a catch in the shipping lanes, and Westro weathers the storm in the North Sea.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head for Coughton Court in Warwickshire. Amongst the items under scrutiny are original designs from one of Britain's leading graphic artists of the 20th century, a bizarre Japanese depiction of skeletons dancing and a lost masterpiece valued at £60,000.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the Fleet Air Arm Museum situated on HMS Heron, the naval aviation base in Yeovilton, Somerset. Paul Martin is joined by experts Charlie Ross and Thomas Plant, and together they pick out a selection of interesting antiques to be sold at a local auction. Paul finds out about one of Europe's largest helicopter squadrons which operates out of HMS heron and takes to the skies. He also goes behind the scenes at the museum, where he meets curator Dave Morris, whose pioneering way of working is bringing exhibits to life in a way never previously imagined.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jake Bhardwaj, Sue Cleaver, Rachel Parris and Rav Wilding take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is on hand with more Strictly exclusives and behind-the-scenes action from the Tower Ballroom. Also, she's joined by a brand new all-star panel to break down the upcoming performances ahead of the weekend’s Blackpool Extravaganza.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Boxing
programme.desc: Having made history to become Wales's first female boxing world champion and cementing herself among the sport's elite, Lauren Price returns to home soil to defend her unified world welterwight titles against Michaela Kotaskova. Catrin Heledd and the team present live coverage from the Cardiff International Arena.

programme.title: The Dead Don’t Hurt
programme.desc: Two pioneers fight for their lives and their love on the American frontier during the Civil War. In English, French, Spanish and Danish with English subtitles.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Warren Arter was seen as a star detective in the Metropolitan Police, but he was also a sexual predator. He used his position running a rape and sexual offences unit to groom and sexually exploit vulnerable women whose cases he investigated. But the Met missed a string of opportunities to stop Arter and then suspended him on full pay for almost seven years before finally dismissing him for drug offences in 2023. In 2024, he was with his wife Rebekah when she died in a hotel room in Barbados in mysterious circumstances. Reporter Noel Titheradge investigates the case that has been called the Met's 'dirty secret' and tracks down new witnesses who tell him what really happened. Could Rebekah's death have been prevented? And why didn't the Met act sooner to stop the predator in its ranks?

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: As their shared enemy finally comes to light, Michael and the Phelans are forced to come together to survive. Meanwhile, a new trauma opens old wounds, pushing Diana towards a decision that will change everything.

programme.desc: Marcus plans to bring in some ducks, but things aren’t as simple as they seem as he heads out onto the lake to create a new home for them. Heading to Devon, he discovers the perfect breed for the smallholding and picks up some top tips and tricks on how to rear them. Back on the farm, the bounty of the kitchen garden inspires a visit to a local community fridge to learn more about how it works, before a neighbour pops over to give him a lesson on what is edible and growing wild in the hedgerows and bushes that surround the smallholding. Once the new ducks arrive and are safely in their new home, he cooks up a fantastic feast inspired by a British classic, the ploughman's lunch.

programme.title: Nadiya’s Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Nadiya shows off her easy celebration bakes, which range from a glittering meringue layer cake to a slow-cooked lamb curry fit for a feast, with an American-inspired seafood extravaganza.

programme.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
programme.desc: Screen adaptation of Oscar Wilde's celebrated play in which two Victorian gentlemen both adopt a double identity under the name of Ernest and end up in trouble when they both turn up at the same country house one weekend.

programme.title: Strangers on a Train
programme.desc: Alfred Hitchcock's suspense classic about two men who plot a perfect murder. When tennis pro Guy Haines meets smooth-talking Bruno Antony in the bar of a train, he finds the stranger sympathetic with his desire to be rid of his clinging wife. The sinister Bruno then proposes that they swap murders: Bruno will murder Guy's wife, and Guy will do away with Bruno's father. From Patricia Highsmith's novel.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The programme comes from the Platform in Morecambe, Lancashire, which in its day was the main station bringing holidaymakers to the town. Antiques experts Charles Hanson and Catherine Southon find treasures to take to auction, including a vintage Rolex watch. Paul Martin discovers the rags-to-riches story of the town's most famous son - Eric Morecambe.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Broadcasting legend Bob Harris and queen of motor sports Suzi Perry burn rubber across south east England in a racy 1974 Ford Escort RS 2000. But can they flip antiques for profit? Steering them in the right direction are doyens Margie Cooper and Raj Bisram, both veteran road trippers and rivals to the core. What starts out as a hunt for music and travel collectibles changes tack very early on. Bob falls for a pair of romantic champagne flutes in a love heart stand, while Suzy steps back in time when she discovers a Japanese glass fishing float. Along the way, they learn to raise their profile through the art of silhouette portraiture, with some amazing results. But at the auction, there can be only one winner. Will Bob reach the number one spot, or will Suzy be racing for the stars?

programme.title: The Eagle Has Landed
programme.desc: All-action World War II adventure. On the morning of 6 November 1943, the military authorities in Berlin receive a simple message - 'The Eagle Has Landed'. In a daring kidnap attempt, a small force of crack German paratroopers are poised to snatch Winston Churchill and return with him to Germany. If they succeed in their mission, it could alter the course of the war. Who can stop them?

programme.title: 40 Hidden Music Treasures at the BBC
programme.desc: A collection of 40 rarely seen musical moments that don't often get to escape from the BBC vaults. Featuring Roachford on The Roland Rat Show, David Bowie on Friday Night with Jonathan Ross, Mary J Blige appearing on Davina McCall's chat show and one of Gloria Estefan's several star turns on the Royal Variety Show over the years.

programme.title: 40 Hidden Music Treasures at the BBC
programme.desc: Another deep dive into the BBC’s music archives, where the musical map is pointed away from Top of the Pops on a quest to uncover 40 rarely seen performances and hidden gems. Featuring Bronski Beat’s first BBC performance of Smalltown Boy, Rihanna’s rockier version of Umbrella, Sophie Ellis-Bextor covering Pulp’s Do You Remember the First Time? and Kate Bush pairing up for a tango during Hounds of Love. These tucked-away treats and many, many more make this a journey that musical fans are certain to treasure.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear explores wellbeing and what it means to live a healthy, balanced life. Presenter Marios Costi shares practical advice on reducing stress, finding calm and making positive changes while meeting inspiring deaf people who are breaking down barriers, building confidence and pursuing their dreams. Marios talks with Avril Langard-Tang, a senior lecturer at the University of Wolverhampton and the first deaf woman to walk solo from John O’Groats to Land’s End. She reflects on her extraordinary 980-mile journey, the physical and emotional challenges she faced and the support she received from the deaf community along the way.

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk’s groundbreaking history of cinema begins. Cunk meets Hollywood legends and interrogates the writer of Die Hard, as she starts her quest deep, deep into cinema. She witnesses the shockingly poor picture quality of the earliest films and marvels at the beards of their Victorian inventors; she gasps audibly at the invention of sound; and she critiques some of the supposedly finest creations of Hollywood’s Golden Age. Along the way she interviews filmmakers, actors and critics, including several you’ve definitely heard of, and she (and you) finally discovers the true meaning of The Wizard of Oz.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: For a live demonstration of terroir, Eva heads to Domaine Dujac, home of the current most-wanted Burgundy wine. Standing on one side of a road, owner Jeremy Seysses points to a parcel of grand cru (the very best) of Clos de la Roche. On the other side is a premier cru (the next best) - a Gevrey-Chambertin Combottes. Back at the winery, Eva tucks into beef cheeks bathed in Domaine Dujac for a classic boeuf bourguignon lunch. Despite the grapes being grown just a few metres away, these reds are a class apart.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Siobhan, her partner Timmie and their two young children hope to bring new life to their small village in Ireland by renovating the old post office to become their forever home. But with funds running low and work grinding to a halt, will their dream family home become a reality?

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear joins BBC Children in Need for a special programme exploring the difference funding makes to the lives of deaf and disabled children, and their families. Featuring inspiring personal stories, a fun lip-reading challenge and the incredible people and organisations helping children build confidence, find friendship and feel they belong. Select ‘sign language’ to watch a version of this programme on iPlayer without the voice over.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family and friends Frankie, James, Susanne and Jason – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Colin Murray and Edith Bowman explore St George’s Market in Belfast and meet a social media sensation who reveals the secrets of healthy and inexpensive one-pot meals. Farmer Jim Smith discovers how one farm is turning its oats into milk, food journalist Leyla Kazim is in Norfolk to find out the secrets of producing mustard, and farmer Meinir Howells reveals just why Welsh lamb is so popular.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's coastal railway journey takes him past lochs and castles on the Far North Line to Britain’s northernmost railway station at Thurso.

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: Karen of Ladram hunts for hake off Cornwall, a rookie crew work in the Irish Sea, trainee skipper Michael steps up in a storm, and Tydus heads out in search of crabs in the North Sea.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team are in Lancaster, where items uncovered include a valuable pair of clogs, a moving series of letters from the Crimea, an anti-slavery ring and a rare and intricately woven tapestry.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Longleat in Wiltshire, home to the seventh Marquess of Bath, where a wide variety of antiques and collectibles are put before experts Claire Rawle and Michael Baggott at the valuation tables, including a stunning amethyst and pearl brooch. But it's an autograph album with a set of Beatles signatures that has the experts guessing. Are they genuine or not? All is revealed at the auction. Paul Martin also takes a trip to London to unearth the hidden architectural gems of one of Wiltshire's most famous sons - Sir Christopher Wren.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jake Bhardwaj, Sue Cleaver, Rachel Parris and Rav Wilding take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is back with the latest news and behind-the-scenes action from the world of Strictly. Also, costume designer Vicky Gill has an exclusive look at what the couples will be wearing in Blackpool's Tower Ballroom.

programme.title: The Emerald Isles
programme.desc: Ardal is in the south of Ireland, where he discovers beautiful Garnish Island, home to gorgeous, lush gardens and the rare white-tailed eagle. By kayak, Ardal sees its thriving seal colony, before heading south to Sherkin Island, where he’s at sea once more, being introduced to a playful pod of dolphins. A local historian tells us of the island’s pirate past, and a resident artist reveals its current status as a painters’ paradise. A short hop takes Ardal to Cape Clear, Ireland’s southernmost island, where he’s taken on a tour in one of the island’s electric buses. He’s introduced to some remarkable standing stones and a gin distillery that uses foraged kelp. The island’s resident ornithologist explains the huge importance of the island for migratory birds. A climactic clifftop view, out across the Atlantic, marks the end to a revealing and unforgettable journey.

programme.title: Barra on the Foyle
programme.desc: Barra Best makes a journey across the 4,000 square kilometres of the Foyle river network, criss-crossing his way across the many rivers and streams that make up its great catchment.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police investigate the disappearance of a young monk from a monastery on a remote private island in Orkney. The mystery deepens when there appears to be no evidence of how he could have left the island. In Aviemore, a rock festival erupts into violence. In Inverness, officers hunt a man after a woman is attacked in a cemetery, while campers in Fort William take a wrong turn.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: By the start of the new millennium, the three chefs had changed British dining forever. This episode follows what happens when the rivalry that made them gets harder to walk away from than to feed, and brings them together for the first time in decades, exploring how each man handled the success he had fought for. Will time have healed old wounds, or will old rivalries still burn brightly?

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk continues her epic journey deep, deep into film. She interrogates some of the world’s foremost filmmakers and critics, discovers an age of screen icons, from Marilyn Monroe to Wayne John, learns how Hollywood movies changed as American social values relaxed, and discovers how, believe it or not, other countries were making films as well. Along the way, she gives her verdict on classics like Jaws, Taxi Driver, and Citizen Ken - very much the Citizen Kane of films about people called Ken.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O’Connell.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: In Portadown, Lee and Sarah keep a careful watch as the pubs and clubs spill out. A man harangues Stephen, accusing him of refusing to take his own mother to the bingo. Eventually, he is sent packing, and Stephen reveals his mother does not play bingo. Back in Belfast, Jade, Tom, Perri and Adam spot a row outside shops where young people say their money has been stolen by a woman. CCTV suggests the man she is with may also have headbutted a passer-by. The man violently resists arrest, fighting, spitting and shouting sectarian abuse at Tom and Adam. By contrast, his partner tries to bond with her arresting officers.

programme.title: Past Lives
programme.desc: Following two childhood friends over the course of 24 years while they contemplate the nature of their relationship as they grow apart, living different lives.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: The standout chefs from the week’s heats battle it out again in the quarter-final. The stakes are higher, the challenges more demanding, and the judges’ expectations are greater than ever.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Irish film star Chris O'Dowd joins Bill Murray and his friend Tom Coyne for a lively round of golf, with enthusiasm occasionally outstripping ability. Away from the fairways, a traditional rambling house takes Bill outside his comfort zone as he explores Ireland's rich storytelling traditions. Later, in a packed Irish pub, the music starts – and staying on the sidelines proves impossible.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A newbie Derbyshire developer admits he's winging it! In Bournemouth, Martin is gobsmacked by the building he's in. Jacqui is in a Norfolk village called Little Snoring, but there's no time for her to take a nap with a property to see.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Briony May Williams helps discerning house hunters from a town in Kent relocate to the quieter countryside of Norfolk and Suffolk. With three dogs and an impressive collection of cars and motorcycles, there’s plenty to accommodate. So, finding a home that’s not too big, not too small, but just right proves quite the challenge. Briony also pulls on her waders in the River Waveney to discover what’s being done to keep its waters clean for wild swimmers.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul are in County Durham, fishing the River Tees for a rare species of wild brown trout. Bob takes Paul on a trip across the landscapes of his youth, navigating the area through the lens of his six-year-old self. Bob lost his dad when he was very young, but some of the memories he holds dear are of the fishing trips they used to go on. Later, Bob invites their old friend Reece Shearsmith to dinner. Reece has some particularly spooky local tales to tell them about the River Tees.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: With the promise of unimaginable computing power, a global race for quantum supremacy is raging. Hannah Fry looks inside the IBM research facility, one of the oldest tech companies in the world, to uncover the future of quantum technology. She explores the unprecedented potential of quantum computing and how precarious this advanced power may be in the wrong hands. Through her exclusive interviews with world-class experts in quantum technologies, Hannah explores the international quantum arms race between the US and China. She breaks down the implications of this 21st-century race and how a quantum future could change the very nature of humanity.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: The European Union's foreign policy chief sits down with Nick in Brussels to discuss her uncompromising stance on Russia, Europe's future relationship with the UK and how her Estonian family's experience under Soviet rule formed her worldview as Europe's top diplomat.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, four colleagues from Colchester Zoo, Lizzie, Kez, Mo and Sue – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher explores the annual Neath food festival and finds out whether traditional or exotic Welsh cakes are more popular among the visitors. Food journalist Leyla Kazim reveals secrets of tomato growing on a large and small scale, while farmer Jim Smith gets stuck into making marmalade. Ryan Hand tries an experiment to find out whether there is such a thing as ‘brain food’.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael crosses over to the Orkney Islands, visiting the former naval base at Scapa Flow and learning about the islands' extensive Norwegian connections.

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: Margaret of Ladram gambles in the Bristol Channel, Emilia Jayne chases a catch in the shipping lanes, and Westro weathers the storm in the North Sea.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head for Coughton Court in Warwickshire. Amongst the items under scrutiny are original designs from one of Britain's leading graphic artists of the 20th century, a bizarre Japanese depiction of skeletons dancing and a lost masterpiece valued at £60,000.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the Fleet Air Arm Museum situated on HMS Heron, the naval aviation base in Yeovilton, Somerset. Paul Martin is joined by experts Charlie Ross and Thomas Plant, and together they pick out a selection of interesting antiques to be sold at a local auction. Paul finds out about one of Europe's largest helicopter squadrons which operates out of HMS heron and takes to the skies. He also goes behind the scenes at the museum, where he meets curator Dave Morris, whose pioneering way of working is bringing exhibits to life in a way never previously imagined.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jake Bhardwaj, Sue Cleaver, Rachel Parris and Rav Wilding take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is on hand with more Strictly exclusives and behind-the-scenes action from the Tower Ballroom. Also, she's joined by a brand new all-star panel to break down the upcoming performances ahead of the weekend’s Blackpool Extravaganza.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham is joined by Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin for another lively, curiosity-fuelled adventure into the wonders of Britain’s wildlife, uncovering nature’s most fascinating secrets and surprising stories. This week, the team dives into some intriguing autumn mysteries: why don’t seals drown? What is the UK’s most deadly mushroom? And what extraordinary creature has the power to keep autumn leaves alive? Expect surprising discoveries, weird and wonderful wildlife facts and plenty of questions along the way!

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty celebrates the rewards of winter gardening - sharing ideas, inspiration and timely jobs to keep gardeners busy now, while reminding us that warmer days lie ahead. At Longmeadow, he has hellebores to plant, peas to sow and practical advice on propagating roses. Sue Kent gets to work on her allotment, where there’s always plenty to do during the colder months, including some clever composting. Jamie Butterworth takes a tour of one of Somerset’s most imaginative topiary gardens. In Belfast, a local community tells the tale of how their once neglected alleyway has become their pride and joy. Carol Klein unearths some radical new thinking on how flowers may be adapting to climate change, while Rekha Mistry travels to RHS Garden Bridgewater to see how garden varieties of tomato and mint are put to the test.

programme.title: Boxing
programme.desc: Having made history to become Wales's first female boxing world champion and cementing herself among the sport's elite, Lauren Price returns to home soil to defend her unified world welterwight titles against Michaela Kotaskova. Catrin Heledd and the team present live coverage from the Cardiff International Arena.

programme.title: The Dead Don’t Hurt
programme.desc: Two pioneers fight for their lives and their love on the American frontier during the Civil War. In English, French, Spanish and Danish with English subtitles.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Warren Arter was seen as a star detective in the Metropolitan Police, but he was also a sexual predator. He used his position running a rape and sexual offences unit to groom and sexually exploit vulnerable women whose cases he investigated. But the Met missed a string of opportunities to stop Arter and then suspended him on full pay for almost seven years before finally dismissing him for drug offences in 2023. In 2024, he was with his wife Rebekah when she died in a hotel room in Barbados in mysterious circumstances. Reporter Noel Titheradge investigates the case that has been called the Met's 'dirty secret' and tracks down new witnesses who tell him what really happened. Could Rebekah's death have been prevented? And why didn't the Met act sooner to stop the predator in its ranks?

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: As their shared enemy finally comes to light, Michael and the Phelans are forced to come together to survive. Meanwhile, a new trauma opens old wounds, pushing Diana towards a decision that will change everything.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Flutter buys a new fishy pet from slippery salesman Mervyn, but the Piripenguins get stuck in its gloopy slime. Can the friends find a solution to their sticky situation?

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Cosima takes over Dad's mission to film a unique underwater plant. But his special camera proves harder to operate than she'd thought, and Big Lizard keeps getting distracted.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy falls in love with a gold watch, but it belongs to the farmer...

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Mr Friendlyface is acting very strangely indeed. He refuses to stamp any of Admin Bunny’s documents, keeps getting distracted by butterflies, and seems oddly happy! The heroes are extremely suspicious and decide that someone must have swapped him with a doppelganger. Now they must quest to find out where the real Friendlyface is and get him back before the forest descends into total chaos.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings lay hands on an ancient console, and Grizzy is transported into the game.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck and Frog are working at a supermarket alongside Toad and Flamingo, who keep ruining Duck and Frog's hard work to make them look bad. Why are they being so mean?

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Roy, Crocalor and Kilowattrel take on Drayton in a spirited rematch.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: The Winx indulge in a day of fun at the amusement park in Magixia but are suddenly attacked by Vexius. This time, however, they may be able to stop him with the help of unexpected allies...

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Meet new BP presenter Leo, who takes to the skies in an incredible skydive challenge to earn his Blue Peter Badge - can he achieve a world record on his very first show?

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall heads to Oman, where he abseils to a verreaux's eagle nest, tracks down wolves and swims alongside a super pod made up of over 100 dolphins.

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: Anita Rani pays a Christmas visit to Baroness Floella Benjamin, a pivotal figure to generations of young TV viewers. Born in Trinidad and Tobago, Floella arrived in London at the age of ten as part of the Windrush generation. Together, they retrace that journey and reflect on Dame Floella's extraordinary life shaped by faith and the festive season: from stage actor and iconic Play School presenter to businesswoman, child rights campaigner, dame and baroness, and even playing a role in King Charles III's coronation.
